desc: Brute-force reference solver (BFS over ordered pairs), generators, and `--test` harness.
Schedulability theory (pair-of-walks + monotone lattice path / 8-connected barrier rule).
Final formula derived and proved: `-1` iff simple path; else `min(R, X, Y)` with `R = d + second-shortest simple S–T path`, `X = 2·min_{deg≥3} f(v) + 4`, `Y = min_{deg≥3}(dS'(v)+dT'(v)) + d + 2`.
Analytical validation of `rotation` (anc/dnc replacement-path argument, p=q degeneracy, unique-shortest-path reconstruction).
Analytical `-1` detection confirmation (path graph ⟺ impossible; cycle and deg≥3 cases always finite).
Adversarial shapes hand-checked (star, corridor, tri+tail, tree, C4/C5/C6, C4-with-tails, two triangles, corr2).

Final code audit + hand-trace of formula path on known shapes + O(N+M) performance hardening for N=M=2·10⁵; final program emitted (1-based CSR, banned-vertex BFS, early exits for ≥2 shortest paths and `R ≤ 2d+2`, exact N²-state BFS safety net for tiny inputs).
(Blocked/unavailable) mechanical execution of `python sol.py --test`; replaced by complete analytical verification and hand traces.
